findings.title: Step 7 tells the agent to call check_plan_conformance()/check_requirement_conformance() but never says to pass depends_on/documents, the two kwargs that make the GOV-010 "Requirement coverage" condition fire.
findings.evidence: .claude/agents/idea-planner.md:84-87 (source agent-workflows/idea-planner-agent.md:68-71). Repro: check_plan_conformance(draft_missing_Requirement_coverage_heading) called with no kwargs → conformant=True, missing=() even though the draft is paired and GOV-010 requires that heading unconditionally when paired.
findings.consequence: An agent instance following the instructions literally (no-arg call) will self-certify a non-conformant paired draft as conformant — the exact failure REQ-014 R20 exists to catch, defeated at the one call site that actually exercises it in production use.

findings.title: GOV-014's Planner "Outputs" line is left unconditional (correctly, per scope), but GOV-014 states it is the authority and the agent definition is updated to match it, and nothing in GOV-014 flags the planner's conditional pairing as a sanctioned, temporary exception.
findings.evidence: docs/08-governance/GOV-014-realization-role-contracts.md:110-111 ("Outputs: a requirement and plan document pair per track") and :26-27 ("this document is the authority and the agent definition is updated to match it, not the reverse").
findings.consequence: A future reader/adversary applying GOV-014's own stated authority literally would be justified in "fixing" idea-planner.md back to unconditional pairing, reverting this phase's owner-approved behavior.
findings.minimal_fix: One line in GOV-014's Planner section noting the pairing exception is deliberate pending the owner's separate GOV-014/ARCH-006 amendment.

findings.title: idea-planner.md has tools Read, Grep, Bash (no Write/Edit), and "How you write the draft" gives no mechanism for safely producing a long Markdown file (tables, code fences, backticks) via Bash.
findings.evidence: Contrast idea-triage.md:103-123, which for a one-line finding explicitly mandates write-to-file-then-$(cat ...) to avoid shell-interpolation corruption.
findings.consequence: The planner's output is far larger and more injection-prone and has no equivalent safeguard.
